html:
SMTO-SSH-0010 — Remote sudo isn't available for this connection

GUID: 2a7ccafe-6735-5dd2-a039-865ed88783a0
Slug: remote-privilege-unsupported
Domain: SSH · Subsystem: remote

What happened

  • SMTO can run sudo on another computer over SSH only from a Linux or macOS Gateway, with a direct SSH connection. This connection goes through a jump server or starts from Windows, so nothing was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the Gateway for this prompt runs on Windows, choose a Gateway on a Linux or macOS computer instead. Remote sudo over SSH isn't supported from a Gateway running on Windows.
  2. Ask the person who manages that Gateway whether its SSH settings reach the computer through a jump server (ProxyJump or ProxyCommand). Use a Gateway that can connect directly. SMTO only sends a sudo password over a direct connection to a computer it has already checked.
  3. On the new Gateway, first have the Agent run a simple SSH command without sudo, then ask for the sudo command again. SMTO must check the computer and account from that Gateway before allowing sudo.

What success looks like

  • The Agent runs the sudo command on the remote computer from the direct Gateway and shows its result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the Gateway. Don't run sudo on the Gateway itself as a workaround; it would act on the wrong computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Remote elevation was refused before dispatch because the Gateway runs on Windows or the effective ssh -G configuration for the destination sets ProxyCommand or ProxyJump.

What this means

  • The remote privilege path rejects Windows or effective ProxyCommand/ProxyJump settings before delivering remote elevation. Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.

Why this can happen

  • The remote privilege path rejects Windows or effective ProxyCommand/ProxyJump settings before delivering remote elevation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the effective SSH routing and platform rather than assuming the sudo password is wrong.

How to fix it

  • _stream refuses remote elevation when settings.platform is windows, and _check_config refuses when ssh -G for the destination reports a ProxyCommand or ProxyJump other than none. Use a POSIX Gateway that can reach the host directly (no proxy routing in its effective SSH configuration), keep the same verified host/user/port, and reissue the elevated ssh command.
  • Use the supported captured POSIX SSH elevation route without unsupported proxy routing; retain exact target verification.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • The requested operation uses a supported verified direct remote elevation route.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
